correctness.rationale: The upper bound follows from Taylor-polynomial approximations to disk automorphisms tested on a single basis vector, giving an exact powered coefficient sum and hence the Kayumov-Ponnusamy infimum obstruction. The p-to-p' symmetry is obtained from Banach adjoint duality together with equality of unilateral forward/backward polynomial-shift norms via bilateral translation. Endpoint norms, strictness away from p=2, and the Hilbert-point asymptotics were checked separately.

originality.rationale: Kania supplies the shift-radius definition and interpolation lower bound, while Kayumov-Ponnusamy supply the scalar powered Bohr theorem. Searches by source title, shift polynomial calculus, powered Bohr radius, dual exponents, and equivalent unilateral Toeplitz/convolution formulations found no prior statement transferring the powered Bohr obstruction to this shift radius or deriving the resulting duality, strictness, endpoint limits, and linear Hilbert-point separation. Known scalar Bohr theory and standard shift transference are excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The result turns a lower-bound-only quantitative question into a two-sided theory, identifies p=2 as the unique full-radius exponent, proves exact dual-exponent symmetry, determines the non-Hilbert endpoint limits, and establishes the exact linear order of the contractivity defect near p=2.
